question: Which statement best describes Unit tests?
options: A test can replace a network service with a controlled response. This makes error and loading cases repeatable. Keep mocks near the boundary so tests still exercise the important UI behavior. For example, a controlled server response can reproduce a 500 error in a component test. In a real page, a mocked 500 response can verify that the UI offers a retry. A mock is like a controlled stand-in used to repeat one difficult situation.

A component test checks what a user can see and do in one interface piece. It can click buttons, type text, and check accessible labels. Prefer user actions over implementation details. For example, a component test can submit an empty form and check the visible field error. In a real page, a component test can select a visible button by its accessible name. A component test is like rehearsing one scene with a real prop and actor.

An end-to-end test follows a real journey in a browser, such as signing in and saving a setting. These tests catch routing and integration failures but take longer to run. For example, an end-to-end test can sign in, change a preference, and reload the page. In a real page, an end-to-end test can cover checkout from cart through confirmation. An end-to-end test is like following a customer’s whole trip through a store.

A unit test checks a small piece of logic, such as a formatter or validation rule. It runs quickly and isolates one behavior. Use clear inputs and expected results, like checking a calculator with known sums. For example, a unit test can verify that a price formatter displays a zero value correctly. In a real page, a unit test can check that a date formatter handles a missing value.

Test the behaviors most likely to harm users or break often. A few dependable tests are more useful than many flaky tests that teams stop trusting. For example, run stable checks in CI and quarantine flaky tests until their cause is understood. In a real page, remove flaky tests from the release gate until their timing is reliable. Test effort is like inspection time: spend more where failure would hurt most.
